candidate_relations.reason: Only mild nuclear sclerosis was present, with no lens trauma, hypermature cataract, pressure elevation, or lens material explaining the culture-positive iris abscess.
The patient had no ocular surgery and symptoms followed dental cleaning, so a postoperative route conflicts with the endogenous Streptococcus intermedius infection.
Anterior-chamber cells, fibrin, and hypopyon constitute severe iritis, but the focal iris granuloma yielding S. intermedius identifies an infectious abscess within endogenous endophthalmitis.
The patient had no systemic instability and blood and urine cultures were negative, so sepsis was not demonstrated despite presumed transient hematogenous ocular spread.
Keratic precipitates and 3+ anterior-chamber cells establish uveitis, but this broad inflammatory label omits the cultured iris abscess and endogenous infection.
